description: A security framework that verifies user and device identities, determines access permissions, and records activity to enforce policies and maintain accountability across networks, applications, and other IT resources.
A set of rules that allows or blocks network traffic based on source and destination IP addresses, protocols, and ports.
Communicating devices continuously monitor their environment for interference and adjust the channel map to address it.
A path-vector exterior gateway protocol that exchanges routing information between autonomous systems and selects paths based on policies and AS-path attributes.
Provides unique identifiers for system configuration issues, facilitating fast and accurate correlation of configuration data across multiple information sources and tools.
a centralized repository that stores information about an organization's IT assets and the relationships between them.
A standardized, machine-readable method for naming and identifying classes of applications, operating systems, and hardware devices within an enterprise’s computing assets.
Detects the unauthorized transmission or disclosure of sensitive data and prevents its occurrence.
A security model in which information is encrypted on the sender’s device and can be decrypted only on the intended recipient’s device.
A Cisco-developed dynamic routing protocol that enables routers to automatically learn and exchange route information within a network.
A method of transmitting radio signals by rapidly changing the carrier frequency among many frequencies.
A common set of policies, practices, and protocols that manage and verify the identities of users and devices accessing applications and resources across organizations.
Designed to search through text input for lines that match a specified pattern.
A physical device that securely manages cryptographic keys and performs encryption, decryption, digital-signature, and authentication functions.
The practice of defining, deploying, and managing infrastructure through code and configuration files rather than manual setup.
A framework of policies and technologies to ensure that the right users have the appropriate access to technology resources.
A service that stores and manages user identities.
Physical objects embedded with sensors, processing ability, software, etc., which connect and exchange data with other devices over the Internet.

A security technology that monitors network traffic to detect and automatically block malicious activity in real time by dropping packets, blocking IP addresses, or terminating suspicious connections.
The temporary granting of privileged permissions for a specific task or time period, after which the permissions are automatically revoked.
A subset of UEM focused on managing and securing mobile devices.
A security method that requires users to verify their identity with at least two distinct factors—something they know, have, or are—before granting access.
Measures the average time from the start of a security incident to its detection.
Measures the average time it takes an organization to respond to and recover from a security incident after detection.
A security framework that verifies users and devices before granting network access, enforcing policies based on identity, device type, location, and security posture.

A networking process that modifies IP addresses in packet headers on routers and/or firewalls, allowing multiple devices on a private network to share a single public IP address when accessing the internet.
A high-speed protocol that lets solid-state drives communicate directly with computers over PCIe.
An authorization framework that lets users grant applications limited access to resources through access tokens without sharing passwords.
A routing technique that directs traffic according to defined policies, rather than only by destination IP and the routing table.
A high-speed interface standard for connecting components such as SSDs and graphics cards to a computer.
A physical location where installed network infrastructure serves as an interface between communicating entities, allowing users to connect to a service provider’s network or cloud services.
An open, simple protocol used by VNC to transmit a remote computer’s screen and relay keyboard and mouse input between systems.
An open XML-based standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between an identity provider and a service provider.

A cloud-delivered architecture that combines networking and security services—such as SD-WAN, secure web gateways, CASB, firewalls, and Zero Trust Network Access—to provide secure access to applications and resources from anywhere.
An open standard (protocol) for automating the provisioning, updating, and deprovisioning of user identities between systems.

A software-based WAN technology that centrally manages connectivity among data centers, cloud services, branch offices, and remote users, routing traffic across internet, MPLS, cellular, and other links to improve performance, availability, and cost efficiency.
A label that identifies a user, device, or workload by its security role or group rather than its IP address.
An authentication system that lets a user sign in once with a trusted identity provider and then access multiple related applications without logging in separately to each one.
A security web gateway that controls, inspects, and protects users’ access to websites and internet applications.
A platform that centrally manages, secures, configures, and monitors endpoints throughout their lifecycle.
A logical subdivision of a physical network into separate Layer 2 networks, or broadcast domains.
A graphical desktop-sharing system that enables users to view and remotely control another computer over a network.

A logically isolated, on-demand pool of shared cloud resources within a public cloud provider’s infrastructure, allowing organizations to run servers, databases, and applications in an isolated secure virtual network.
An overlay network using virtualization to extend a private network across a public network, via the use of encryption and tunneling protocols.
A technology that allows multiple instances of a routing table to co-exist within the same router at the same time.
A security control that inspects HTTP/HTTPS traffic to protect web applications from attacks that traditional network firewalls may not detect.
